questions.question: Which register is described as a 16‑bit pointer used for subroutine calls?
questions.explanation: The diagram labels a 16‑bit register as “stack pointer; pointer;; (16)” indicating its role as the stack pointer. (Source Page: [1])

questions.question: What is the width of the internal data bus in the shown architecture?
questions.explanation: The text explicitly mentions an “8‑bit Internal Data Bus.” (Source Page: [1])

questions.question: Which component is responsible for selecting among multiple 8‑bit inputs?
questions.explanation: The diagram repeatedly shows a “Multiplexer(8)(8)(8)” which combines three 8‑bit sources. (Source Page: [1])

questions.question: According to the logic‑instruction rules, which flag is NOT cleared by a complement instruction?
questions.explanation: Rule 2 states that all logic instructions clear the carry flag except complement, where the flag remains unchanged. (Source Page: [18])

questions.question: In the described micro‑architecture, where is the result of a logic instruction placed?
questions.explanation: Rule 4 of the logic‑instruction features says “Place the result in the accumulator.” (Source Page: [18])

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed as a flag modified by logic instructions?
questions.explanation: Rule 3 mentions that Z, P, and S flags are modified, while the carry flag is cleared (or left unchanged for complement). (Source Page: [18])

questions.question: The “Program Counter” in the diagram has which of the following characteristics?

options.A: 8‑bit width and used for arithmetic results
options.C: 8‑bit width and serves as a stack pointer
options.D: 16‑bit width and functions as a temporary register

questions.explanation: The diagram labels “Program Counter (16)” together with an Incrementer/Decrementer, indicating a 16‑bit counter that advances automatically. (Source Page: [1])

questions.question: Which control signal is associated with serial I/O according to the diagram?
questions.explanation: The text lists “Interrupt Control Serial I/O Control” as separate items, indicating a dedicated serial I/O control signal. (Source Page: [1])

questions.question: Which component directly follows the “Logic Decoder” in the data path?
questions.explanation: The diagram shows “Logic Decoder 3 D_ (8) E (8) > (ALU)Unit,” indicating the ALU receives the decoded signals. (Source Page: [1])

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the accumulator in this architecture is true?

options.A: It is a 16‑bit register used for address calculations.
options.B: It automatically clears the Zero flag after every operation.
options.C: It is one of the implicit operands for all logic instructions.
options.D: It functions as the stack pointer for subroutine calls.

questions.explanation: Rule 1 of the logic‑instruction features states that “The instructions implicitly assume that the accumulator is one of the operands.” (Source Page: [18])
